# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

"""Estimate elastic modulus from tensile stress-strain data via linear least squares.

Usage: python analyze.py [measurements.csv]
Writes results.csv and modulus_fits.png next to the input file.
"""
import csv
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

MATERIALS = ["aluminum", "steel", "titanium"]
# Categorical slots 1-3 of the reference palette (validated all-pairs, light mode)
COLORS = {"aluminum": "#2a78d6", "steel": "#eb6834", "titanium": "#1baf7a"}
MARKERS = {"aluminum": "o", "steel": "s", "titanium": "^"}
TEXT, TEXT_2, GRID, SURFACE = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#e4e3df", "#fcfcfb"


def linfit(x, y):
    """OLS fit y = m*x + b. Returns slope, intercept, slope std. error, R^2."""
    x, y = np.asarray(x), np.asarray(y)
    n = len(x)
    m, b = np.polyfit(x, y, 1)
    resid = y - (m * x + b)
    s2 = resid @ resid / (n - 2)
    se_m = np.sqrt(s2 / np.sum((x - x.mean()) ** 2))
    r2 = 1 - resid @ resid / np.sum((y - y.mean()) ** 2)
    return m, b, se_m, r2


def main(path):
    path = Path(path)
    data = defaultdict(lambda: ([], []))
    material_of = {}
    with path.open() as f:
        for row in csv.DictReader(f):
            data[row["specimen"]][0].append(float(row["strain"]))
            data[row["specimen"]][1].append(float(row["stress_mpa"]))
            material_of[row["specimen"]] = row["material"]

    rows = []
    # Per-specimen fits (slope in MPa -> report GPa)
    for spec in sorted(data):
        x, y = data[spec]
        m, b, se, r2 = linfit(x, y)
        m0 = np.dot(x, y) / np.dot(x, x)  # through-origin check
        rows.append(dict(level="specimen", material=material_of[spec], specimen=spec,
                         n=len(x), E_gpa=m / 1e3, E_se_gpa=se / 1e3,
                         intercept_mpa=b, r2=r2, E_origin_gpa=m0 / 1e3))

    # Pooled fit per material + spread of specimen estimates
    summary = {}
    for mat in MATERIALS:
        specs = [s for s in sorted(data) if material_of[s] == mat]
        x = np.concatenate([data[s][0] for s in specs])
        y = np.concatenate([data[s][1] for s in specs])
        m, b, se, r2 = linfit(x, y)
        m0 = np.dot(x, y) / np.dot(x, x)
        spec_E = np.array([r["E_gpa"] for r in rows if r["material"] == mat])
        summary[mat] = dict(m=m, b=b, x=x, y=y, specs=specs, spec_E=spec_E)
        rows.append(dict(level="pooled", material=mat, specimen="+".join(specs),
                         n=len(x), E_gpa=m / 1e3, E_se_gpa=se / 1e3,
                         intercept_mpa=b, r2=r2, E_origin_gpa=m0 / 1e3,
                         spec_mean_gpa=spec_E.mean(), spec_sd_gpa=spec_E.std(ddof=1)))

    out_csv = path.with_name("results.csv")
    fields = ["level", "material", "specimen", "n", "E_gpa", "E_se_gpa", "intercept_mpa",
              "r2", "E_origin_gpa", "spec_mean_gpa", "spec_sd_gpa"]
    with out_csv.open("w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fields)
        w.writeheader()
        for r in rows:
            w.writerow({k: (f"{v:.4g}" if isinstance(v, float) else v) for k, v in r.items()})

    for r in rows:
        extra = (f"  specimens: {r['spec_mean_gpa']:.1f} ± {r['spec_sd_gpa']:.1f}"
                 if r["level"] == "pooled" else "")
        print(f"{r['level']:8s} {r['material']:9s} {r['specimen']:14s} "
              f"E={r['E_gpa']:7.2f} ± {r['E_se_gpa']:.2f} GPa  b={r['intercept_mpa']:+6.2f} MPa  "
              f"R²={r['r2']:.5f}  E0={r['E_origin_gpa']:.2f}{extra}")

    plot(summary, path.with_name("modulus_fits.png"))


def style(ax):
    ax.set_facecolor(SURFACE)
    for s in ("top", "right"):
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
    for s in ("left", "bottom"):
        ax.spines[s].set_color(GRID)
    ax.tick_params(colors=TEXT_2, labelsize=9, length=0, pad=6)
    ax.grid(True, color=GRID, linewidth=0.8)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)


def plot(summary, out):
    fig, (ax, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4.8), facecolor=SURFACE,
                                  gridspec_kw=dict(width_ratios=[1.7, 1]))
    style(ax)
    style(ax2)

    xs = np.linspace(0, 0.0021, 50)
    for mat in MATERIALS:
        s = summary[mat]
        c = COLORS[mat]
        ax.scatter(s["x"] * 100, s["y"], s=40, marker=MARKERS[mat], color=c,
                   edgecolor=SURFACE, linewidth=1.2, zorder=3, label=mat.capitalize())
        ax.plot(xs * 100, s["m"] * xs + s["b"], color=c, linewidth=2, zorder=2)
        ax.annotate(f"{mat.capitalize()}  E = {s['m'] / 1e3:.1f} GPa",
                    xy=(0.21, s["m"] * 0.0021 + s["b"]), xytext=(6, 0),
                    textcoords="offset points", va="center", fontsize=9.5, color=TEXT)
    ax.set_xlim(0, 0.21)
    ax.set_ylim(0, None)
    ax.set_xlabel("Strain (%)", color=TEXT_2, fontsize=10)
    ax.set_ylabel("Stress (MPa)", color=TEXT_2, fontsize=10)
    ax.set_title("Stress–strain data with pooled linear fits", loc="left",
                 color=TEXT, fontsize=11.5, pad=10)
    ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper left", fontsize=9, labelcolor=TEXT)

    # Right panel: specimen-level moduli, mean ± SD
    for i, mat in enumerate(MATERIALS):
        E = summary[mat]["spec_E"]
        c = COLORS[mat]
        jitter = np.array([-0.08, 0, 0.08])[: len(E)]
        ax2.errorbar(i, E.mean(), yerr=E.std(ddof=1), color=TEXT_2, capsize=5,
                     linewidth=1.2, zorder=2)
        ax2.plot([i - 0.18, i + 0.18], [E.mean()] * 2, color=TEXT_2, linewidth=2, zorder=2)
        ax2.scatter(i + jitter, E, s=48, marker=MARKERS[mat], color=c,
                    edgecolor=SURFACE, linewidth=1.2, zorder=3)
        ax2.annotate(f"{E.mean():.1f} ± {E.std(ddof=1):.1f}", xy=(i + 0.22, E.mean()),
                     va="center", fontsize=9, color=TEXT)
    ax2.set_xticks(range(len(MATERIALS)), [m.capitalize() for m in MATERIALS])
    ax2.set_xlim(-0.5, 2.9)
    ax2.set_ylim(0, 230)
    ax2.set_ylabel("Elastic modulus (GPa)", color=TEXT_2, fontsize=10)
    ax2.set_title("Per-specimen modulus (mean ± SD, n = 3)", loc="left",
                  color=TEXT, fontsize=11.5, pad=10)

    fig.tight_layout(w_pad=3)
    fig.savefig(out, dpi=200, facecolor=SURFACE)
    print(f"wrote {out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "measurements.csv")

    """OLS fit y = m*x + b. Returns slope, intercept, slope std. error, R^2."""
    x, y = np.asarray(x), np.asarray(y)
    n = len(x)
    m, b = np.polyfit(x, y, 1)
    resid = y - (m * x + b)
    s2 = resid @ resid / (n - 2)
    se_m = np.sqrt(s2 / np.sum((x - x.mean()) ** 2))
    r2 = 1 - resid @ resid / np.sum((y - y.mean()) ** 2)
    return m, b, se_m, r2

"""Estimate elastic modulus from tensile stress-strain data via linear least squares.

Usage: python analyze.py [measurements.csv]
Writes results.csv and modulus_fits.png next to the input file.
"""
import csv
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

MATERIALS = ["aluminum", "steel", "titanium"]
# Categorical slots 1-3 of the reference palette (validated all-pairs, light mode)
COLORS = {"aluminum": "#2a78d6", "steel": "#eb6834", "titanium": "#1baf7a"}
MARKERS = {"aluminum": "o", "steel": "s", "titanium": "^"}
TEXT, TEXT_2, GRID, SURFACE = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#e4e3df", "#fcfcfb"


def linfit(x, y):
    """OLS fit y = m*x + b. Returns slope, intercept, slope std. error, R^2."""
    x, y = np.asarray(x), np.asarray(y)
    n = len(x)
    m, b = np.polyfit(x, y, 1)
    resid = y - (m * x + b)
    s2 = resid @ resid / (n - 2)
    se_m = np.sqrt(s2 / np.sum((x - x.mean()) ** 2))
    r2 = 1 - resid @ resid / np.sum((y - y.mean()) ** 2)
    return m, b, se_m, r2


def main(path):
    path = Path(path)
    data = defaultdict(lambda: ([], []))
    material_of = {}
    with path.open() as f:
        for row in csv.DictReader(f):
            data[row["specimen"]][0].append(float(row["strain"]))
            data[row["specimen"]][1].append(float(row["stress_mpa"]))
            material_of[row["specimen"]] = row["material"]

    rows = []
    # Per-specimen fits (slope in MPa -> report GPa)
    for spec in sorted(data):
        x, y = data[spec]
        m, b, se, r2 = linfit(x, y)
        m0 = np.dot(x, y) / np.dot(x, x)  # through-origin check
        rows.append(dict(level="specimen", material=material_of[spec], specimen=spec,
                         n=len(x), E_gpa=m / 1e3, E_se_gpa=se / 1e3,
                         intercept_mpa=b, r2=r2, E_origin_gpa=m0 / 1e3))

    # Pooled fit per material + spread of specimen estimates
    summary = {}
    for mat in MATERIALS:
        specs = [s for s in sorted(data) if material_of[s] == mat]
        x = np.concatenate([data[s][0] for s in specs])
        y = np.concatenate([data[s][1] for s in specs])
        m, b, se, r2 = linfit(x, y)
        m0 = np.dot(x, y) / np.dot(x, x)
        spec_E = np.array([r["E_gpa"] for r in rows if r["material"] == mat])
        summary[mat] = dict(m=m, b=b, x=x, y=y, specs=specs, spec_E=spec_E)
        rows.append(dict(level="pooled", material=mat, specimen="+".join(specs),
                         n=len(x), E_gpa=m / 1e3, E_se_gpa=se / 1e3,
                         intercept_mpa=b, r2=r2, E_origin_gpa=m0 / 1e3,
                         spec_mean_gpa=spec_E.mean(), spec_sd_gpa=spec_E.std(ddof=1)))

    out_csv = path.with_name("results.csv")
    fields = ["level", "material", "specimen", "n", "E_gpa", "E_se_gpa", "intercept_mpa",
              "r2", "E_origin_gpa", "spec_mean_gpa", "spec_sd_gpa"]
    with out_csv.open("w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fields)
        w.writeheader()
        for r in rows:
            w.writerow({k: (f"{v:.4g}" if isinstance(v, float) else v) for k, v in r.items()})

    for r in rows:
        extra = (f"  specimens: {r['spec_mean_gpa']:.1f} ± {r['spec_sd_gpa']:.1f}"
                 if r["level"] == "pooled" else "")
        print(f"{r['level']:8s} {r['material']:9s} {r['specimen']:14s} "
              f"E={r['E_gpa']:7.2f} ± {r['E_se_gpa']:.2f} GPa  b={r['intercept_mpa']:+6.2f} MPa  "
              f"R²={r['r2']:.5f}  E0={r['E_origin_gpa']:.2f}{extra}")

    plot(summary, path.with_name("modulus_fits.png"))


def style(ax):
    ax.set_facecolor(SURFACE)
    for s in ("top", "right"):
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
    for s in ("left", "bottom"):
        ax.spines[s].set_color(GRID)
    ax.tick_params(colors=TEXT_2, labelsize=9, length=0, pad=6)
    ax.grid(True, color=GRID, linewidth=0.8)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)


def plot(summary, out):
    fig, (ax, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4.8), facecolor=SURFACE,
                                  gridspec_kw=dict(width_ratios=[1.7, 1]))
    style(ax)
    style(ax2)

    xs = np.linspace(0, 0.0021, 50)
    for mat in MATERIALS:
        s = summary[mat]
        c = COLORS[mat]
        ax.scatter(s["x"] * 100, s["y"], s=40, marker=MARKERS[mat], color=c,
                   edgecolor=SURFACE, linewidth=1.2, zorder=3, label=mat.capitalize())
        ax.plot(xs * 100, s["m"] * xs + s["b"], color=c, linewidth=2, zorder=2)
        ax.annotate(f"{mat.capitalize()}  E = {s['m'] / 1e3:.1f} GPa",
                    xy=(0.21, s["m"] * 0.0021 + s["b"]), xytext=(6, 0),
                    textcoords="offset points", va="center", fontsize=9.5, color=TEXT)
    ax.set_xlim(0, 0.21)
    ax.set_ylim(0, None)
    ax.set_xlabel("Strain (%)", color=TEXT_2, fontsize=10)
    ax.set_ylabel("Stress (MPa)", color=TEXT_2, fontsize=10)
    ax.set_title("Stress–strain data with pooled linear fits", loc="left",
                 color=TEXT, fontsize=11.5, pad=10)
    ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper left", fontsize=9, labelcolor=TEXT)

    # Right panel: specimen-level moduli, mean ± SD
    for i, mat in enumerate(MATERIALS):
        E = summary[mat]["spec_E"]
        c = COLORS[mat]
        jitter = np.array([-0.08, 0, 0.08])[: len(E)]
        ax2.errorbar(i, E.mean(), yerr=E.std(ddof=1), color=TEXT_2, capsize=5,
                     linewidth=1.2, zorder=2)
        ax2.plot([i - 0.18, i + 0.18], [E.mean()] * 2, color=TEXT_2, linewidth=2, zorder=2)
        ax2.scatter(i + jitter, E, s=48, marker=MARKERS[mat], color=c,
                    edgecolor=SURFACE, linewidth=1.2, zorder=3)
        ax2.annotate(f"{E.mean():.1f} ± {E.std(ddof=1):.1f}", xy=(i + 0.22, E.mean()),
                     va="center", fontsize=9, color=TEXT)
    ax2.set_xticks(range(len(MATERIALS)), [m.capitalize() for m in MATERIALS])
    ax2.set_xlim(-0.5, 2.9)
    ax2.set_ylim(0, 230)
    ax2.set_ylabel("Elastic modulus (GPa)", color=TEXT_2, fontsize=10)
    ax2.set_title("Per-specimen modulus (mean ± SD, n = 3)", loc="left",
                  color=TEXT, fontsize=11.5, pad=10)

    fig.tight_layout(w_pad=3)
    fig.savefig(out, dpi=200, facecolor=SURFACE)
    print(f"wrote {out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "measurements.csv")

# Elastic modulus from tensile test data

**Data:** `measurements.csv`. There are 9 specimens, 3 each of aluminum, steel and titanium. Each specimen has 10 stress–strain points spaced evenly from 0.02% to 0.20% strain.
**Method:** For each specimen I fit stress = E·strain + b by ordinary least squares and took the slope as the elastic modulus E. I also pooled each material's 30 points and fit them together. Everything is reproducible with `python analyze.py measurements.csv`, which needs numpy and matplotlib.

## Results

| Material | E, pooled fit (GPa) | E, specimen mean ± SD (GPa) | 95% CI on mean (GPa) | Typical handbook value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Aluminum | 69.4 | 69.4 ± 1.8 | 65.0 – 73.7 | ~69–70 (Al alloys) |
| Steel | 199.1 | 199.1 ± 2.0 | 194.1 – 204.0 | ~200 (carbon/alloy steel) |
| Titanium | 116.6 | 116.6 ± 1.7 | 112.3 – 120.8 | ~105–120 (CP Ti / Ti‑6Al‑4V) |

The confidence interval is a t‑interval with n = 3 specimens (t = 4.30). All three moduli fall within normal handbook ranges for these materials.

![Stress–strain data with fits, and specimen-to-specimen scatter](modulus_fits.png)

### Per-specimen fits

| Specimen | E (GPa) | Std. error of slope (GPa) | Intercept (MPa) | R² |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AL-1 | 70.1 | 0.57 | −0.8 | 0.9995 |
| AL-2 | 67.4 | 0.84 | +0.9 | 0.9988 |
| AL-3 | 70.6 | 0.75 | −1.0 | 0.9991 |
| ST-1 | 201.2 | 2.45 | −1.5 | 0.9988 |
| ST-2 | 197.3 | 2.62 | +1.2 | 0.9986 |
| ST-3 | 198.7 | 2.86 | +2.2 | 0.9984 |
| TI-1 | 114.6 | 1.91 | −0.0 | 0.9978 |
| TI-2 | 117.8 | 1.64 | −2.2 | 0.9985 |
| TI-3 | 117.2 | 1.50 | −0.1 | 0.9987 |

The complete output, including fits forced through the origin, is in `results.csv`.

## Notes and caveats

- **The data look linear.** Every fit has R² ≥ 0.998. The intercepts are all within ±2.2 MPa of zero, so there is no sign of a toe region or a seating offset. I also tried adding a quadratic term, and it was not significant for any material (|t| ≤ 1.3). That fits with the whole dataset being below 0.2% strain, which is presumably inside the elastic region. Forcing the fits through the origin changes E by at most 1.6 GPa, so the conclusions don't depend on that choice.
- **Aluminum shows real specimen-to-specimen variation.** AL-2 is about 2.9% below the aluminum mean. That gap is roughly 3–4× its own fit standard error, so it is unlikely to be noise from the fit alone. Possible causes are a real difference in the material, or a cross-section or extensometer error for that specimen. For steel and titanium, the spread between specimens is about what the fit uncertainty alone would produce.
- **Uncertainty.** The slope standard errors from the pooled fits (0.5, 1.5 and 1.0 GPa) treat all 30 points as independent. They therefore understate the true uncertainty because they ignore variation between specimens. The specimen-level SD and the 95% CI are the more honest measures. With only 3 specimens per material, the CIs are wide, about ±4–5 GPa.
- **What's not known from the data.** The file doesn't say which alloy or grade each material is, or how strain was measured. The handbook comparison above is therefore only a sanity check, not a validation.
